claim.pdf_says: Each character-position table (general rules 7 through 11) has a bold header row 'Character Positions | Contents' followed by its data rows, e.g. '1-4 Four numeric characters of the year in the Gregorian calendar.'
claim.markdown_says:
Character Positions Contents

| 1-4 | Four numeric characters of the year in the Gregorian calendar. |
|---|---|
claim.why_it_matters: The printed header row is a loose paragraph outside each table, and each table's first data row is promoted to the markdown header row. The data is all present, so meaning is preserved, but the table structure differs from the printed one.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (p486, folio 462) shows each GR 8-11 table as a bold 'Character Positions   Contents' heading line followed by position/contents rows. The markdown carries the same heading text ('Character Positions Contents') immediately before each table and every data row with identical text. All words are present and in order; the only difference is markdown table formatting (header text as a paragraph, first data row in the pipe-table header slot). That is formatting only and does not change meaning, so it is not a content discrepancy. (The GR11 TIME table's broken 5-6 a)/b) and 7-8 rows are a separate matter not covered by this claim.)
